base_intake.interpretation: Canonical base intake is the preserved broad discovery baseline. It is not treated as a historical completeness proof.

within_year_temporal_skew_audit.diagnostic_slices: calendar quarters and months; audit-only, not publication units
within_year_temporal_skew_audit.assessment: No catastrophic temporal hole is visible in the base arXiv intake. Every month contains more than 2,500 unique papers. Q4 is densest and Q1 sparsest; the material completeness risk is capped cs.LG slices plus present-day publisher-index archival loss, not an empty calendar interval.

arxiv_cap_audit.assessment: Six month/category slices hit the configured 2,000-result ceiling, all in cs.LG. Base arXiv success therefore cannot establish research completeness; material annual anchors are checked by exact identity before Selection.

source_planes.notes: Base intake preserves Scaling Laws, GPT-3/Few-Shot Learners, the OpenAI API launch and the Microsoft GPT-3 licensing boundary. Turing-NLG is a material independent scale/access boundary outside the normalized base official feed and requires first-party gap-fill.

Base intake preserves REALM, Dense Passage Retrieval and RAG primary papers. Meta's first-party RAG release/integration announcement is a distinct deployment/reuse boundary and is added as supplemental evidence.
Base intake preserves Meena and the BlenderBot/Recipes primary papers. Meta's BlenderBot open-source release boundary is not represented as a normalized dated base event and requires gap-fill.

Base intake preserves DDPM, DDIM, score-based generative modeling, Taming Transformers, Jukebox and Image GPT first-party material. These establish the transition beyond text-only autoregressive generation without requiring duplicate gap-fill.
Base intake preserves Learning to summarize from human feedback and the corresponding OpenAI first-party publication, establishing an early explicit human-feedback steering layer.
Base intake contains StereoSet, RealToxicityPrompts and CrowS-Pairs. They are treated as representative evaluation/risk anchors rather than a census of every 2020 benchmark.
Base intake preserves GShard and The Pile, but the material 2020 DeepSpeed/ZeRO open-source training-system release is outside the normalized first-party feed surface and requires gap-fill.

residual_limitations: Present-day official index snapshots cannot prove that every 2020 publisher item remains linked or unchanged.
Six capped cs.LG month slices may omit non-headline research; exact checks protect material editorial anchors but do not make the full research intake exhaustive.

The configured GitHub Release watchlist targets projects material mainly in later years and yields no normalized 2020 release records; commit-level ecosystem history is not reconstructed exhaustively.

Some first-party pages have moved or been edited since 2020; supplemental capture establishes recoverable publisher-defined release/access boundaries, not independent reproduction of capability claims.
Representative bias/toxicity benchmarks are retained to establish the trajectory without claiming an exhaustive 2020 safety-evaluation census.

single_volume_preliminary_assessment.rationale: The year presents a coherent annual arc: scaling becomes an explicit design principle; GPT-3 makes few-shot behavior and model access central; retrieval, dialogue, human-feedback steering, distributed training and new generative-media paradigms emerge around the model. These trajectories interact strongly enough for one annual synthesis and lead naturally into 2021's multi-layer model ecosystem. No H1/H2 split trigger is visible at coverage-audit stage.
